note: Judged on scratch copy serve-anywhere-1001 with its own home (a registry naming only the copy), served on the assigned :4738 from a temp directory with no .walkdown at or above it. Mid-run registration imported a copy of example/ into that home, never the real registry.

results.reasoning: Started from a temp directory belonging to no project, walkdown serve came up and said 'every blueprint registered on this machine (1)' and that it was started outside a registered project. With no blueprint named, /api/blueprint answered key null with the one registered blueprint listed and no rows; the root page drew the Which project? chooser listing what was registered and no rules (root-chooser.png). /api/threads with no name was a 404 saying to name one with ?bp=<id>; ?bp=blueprint served all 156 rules as a server in that project would. A copy of the example project imported into the same home while the server ran was claimed for http://localhost:4310/index.html by the next whose lookup, having matched nothing before, and the chooser then listed both; a screen appended to that copy's storyboard while it ran was claimed on the very next lookup too. Restarted inside the scratch project, a request naming none got that project's blueprint; started outside with --blueprint example, it got the example's nine rules; --blueprint nobody refused with exit 2 and named walkdown blueprints. Every step held as worded.
